title: Actuary Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert an actuary salary from hourly to annual using the 38-hour week, plus tax, super, and fortnightly pay. Official Fair Work and ABS data.

faqs.q: How is an actuary salary calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week as per the National Employment Standards. For example, $60/hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $118,560 per year. This is a gross figure before tax and super. If you work part-time or irregular hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for actuaries?
faqs.a: Casual employees under awards like the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. For actuaries, if your award or agreement includes casual loading, you should not include it in the base rate you enter into a calculator. Instead, use the base rate and apply the loading separately. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides that list the correct casual rates for each classification.

faqs.q: How does tax affect an actuary's take-home pay?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. A 2% Medicare levy generally applies. For an annual actuary salary of $118,560, the tax would be approximately $26,867 plus Medicare levy of $2,371, leaving a take-home of about $89,322 per year. These are estimates and do not include HELP repayments or the Medicare levy surcharge.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert an Hourly Rate to an Annual Actuary Salary

If you are an actuary or considering a career in actuarial work, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual pay is essential. Whether you are negotiating a salary offer or comparing contract rates, the formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This article uses official data from the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), and the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) to guide you through the process, including tax, superannuation, and the fortnightly pay cycle.

### The 38-Hour Week and the Fortnight

Most full-time employees in Australia work a standard 38-hour week under the National Employment Standards. When converting an hourly rate to an annual actuary salary, we assume 38 hours per week unless you know your actual hours are different. For example, if your hourly rate is $60, the calculation is:

- Weekly pay: $60 × 38 = $2,280
- Fortnightly pay: $2,280 × 2 = $4,560
- Annual gross pay: $60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560

Using the fortnightly figure can help with budgeting, as many employers pay fortnightly. Remember that this assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, actuaries are typically covered by the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award [MA000019] or a relevant enterprise agreement. According to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides, award rates for professional roles like actuaries are higher than the minimum wage. The pay guides list minimum rates for each classification, including allowances and penalty rates. Always check the correct award or agreement for your specific role.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual actuary, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, if the base rate is $60, the casual rate would be $75 per hour. When using our [timesheet](/), enter the base hourly rate (without loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox to apply the 25% increase. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading, as this would double-count it. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page provides more details.

### Tax and Superannuation

Your annual actuary salary is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the ATO resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: 45% on the excess over $190,000

A 2% Medicare levy generally applies. For an annual gross salary of $118,560, the tax estimate is approximately $26,867 plus Medicare levy of $2,371, leaving a take-home of about $89,322 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary by your employer. For $118,560, that would be an additional $14,227.20 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not deducted from your pay but is an extra benefit. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Actuary Salary Insights from Official Sources

According to Jobs and Skills Australia, there were approximately 2,400 actuaries employed in Australia as of the 2021 Census, with a median age of 33 years and 89% working full-time. The ABS Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours (May 2025) does not provide median weekly earnings for actuaries due to sample size limitations, but the average weekly earnings for all full-time adult employees was $2,083.70 as of May 2026. Actuaries typically work in financial and insurance services or professional, scientific and technical services. For more data, visit the [reference tables](/data) on occupation profiles.

### Using the Hourly to Annual Conversion

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool helps you quickly see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents of any hourly rate. Remember that the annual figure is an estimate based on consistent hours and no unpaid overtime. If you have an enterprise agreement, your pay may differ from the award minimums. Always refer to your specific employment contract or the relevant [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Summary

Converting an hourly rate to an annual actuary salary is simple: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a standard full-time role, use 38 hours. Include casual loading if applicable, and remember that tax and super are calculated separately. Official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman, ABS, and ATO provide the most reliable figures. Use our tools to estimate your take-home pay and super contributions, and always check your award or agreement for the exact rates.
